subject: Exec brief: payoff matrix, risks, and procurement lane for Veridian Health pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>, Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:13:00 -0800
Subject: Exec brief: payoff matrix, risks, and procurement lane for Veridian Health pilot

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Per our conversation I wanted to capture a concise executive-level brief so your leadership can see the outcomes, the key risks we flagged, and the procurement lane we expect for a 6–8 week pilot. I kept this intentionally short; attached is a one-page payoff matrix and a SOC2 evidence summary.

Top pain points you emphasized
- Batch processing latency spikes in clinical ingestion pipelines causing downstream SLA misses (p95 > 2s at peak)
- High cost and operational burden running legacy LLM deployments in-house
- Security/compliance: need for audit logs and customer-managed keying for PHI-adjacent workflows

Goals we agreed on for a 6-week pilot
- Validate end-to-end inference latency under realistic load (target p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms)
- Demonstrate 30–40% unit-cost reduction via batching + prefix caching by measuring token cost in pilot workload
- Prove integration with your EHR ingestion (redaction + minimal residency) and verify audit log delivery to your SIEM

Payoff matrix (attached spreadsheet summarizes numbers)
- Conservative: 20% cost reduction, p95 = 450–500ms
- Expected: 35% cost reduction, p95 = 300–400ms
- Upside: 55% cost reduction with quantization + longer prefix caching in steady state

Key risks and mitigations
- Data residency: We can run Private deployment in your VPC for pilot if needed (adds 1–2 weeks).
- Security review: we will provide SOC2 artifacts and an architecture diagram; recommend scheduling a technical deep-dive with your InfoSec.
- SLA/fallback: we propose a canary fallback to a smaller verified model during spikes; ops playbook included in the Drive link.

Procurement lane & timeline
- Pilot contract: 6-week fixed-scope PO, estimated commitment $45k (detailed in payoff matrix).
- Approvals: Procurement needs SOW + SOC2 evidence. Expected procurement lead time 4–8 weeks depending on legal redlines.
- Next milestones:
  1) Confirm pilot scope and PO owner by 2026-11-25
  2) Technical kickoff + demo environment access by 2026-11-30
  3) Security review artifacts delivered by 2026-11-25 (we will deliver SOC2 summary attached)

Asks / Decisions for your leadership
- Can you confirm procurement contact for PO (name + email)?
- Do you want the pilot in our Hosted environment (fastest) or Private (VPC) for initial testing? Private adds ~1 week.
- Are the pilot success criteria above aligned to your business sponsor (reduction in cost per inference, target latency)?

Attachments: 20261122-veridian-payoff-matrix.xlsx, soc2-evidence-summary.pdf

Happy to adjust if leadership prefers a shorter memo. If I'm missing anyone on your side who should see this (procurement, InfoSec), please loop them in.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@veridianhealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@veridianhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec brief: payoff matrix, risks, and procurement lane for Veridian Health pilot

Jordan —

Thanks for the concise brief and the attachments; this is exactly what I needed to bring to our CIO. A few clarifications from our side before I share more broadly:

1) Logs/residency: we need confirmation that audit logs can be forwarded to our Splunk instance and that customer-managed keys (KMS) are supported for any PHI-adjacent artifacts.
2) Performance: the p50/p95 targets look good — can you demonstrate p95 < 400ms during the pilot under a 200 TPS simulated load?
3) Pilot cost: the $45k estimate — can you break down engineering vs compute vs support line items (simple table)? We will need that for our Finance PO packet.

Procurement contact: please work with Maya Singh (maya.singh@veridianhealth.com). She owns vendor onboarding and will shepherd the PO.

Security artifacts: SOC2 summary looks good at first pass; we will still require a short technical Q&A next Wed (2026-11-25). Can we schedule a 45-minute slot 09:00–10:00 PT? Tom and I will attend.

If you can provide a short slide (1–2 pages) that ties the payoff matrix to clinical SLA risk reduction, that will help our CIO quickly approve.

Elena
SVP, Digital Transformation
Veridian Health
elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com | +1 212-555-8189
